What the product's own data give is a point-of-sale discount, not a net: CMS Medicare Part D 2024 (drug_demand) records $69,712,635.09 over 582,380 dosage units, $119.70 a tablet, against the $123.05 WAC a tablet then in force ($22,149.25 / 180 from the North Dakota filing), 2.7% off list. That 2.7% cannot stand as gross_to_net_pct, because CMS Part D spending is gross of every manufacturer rebate and of 340B, which is exactly what this key is meant to deduct; carrying it would claim Krazati keeps 97% of WAC. It is a floor on the discount and nothing more. So the filed company figure stays, with its direction stated: net revenue per patient here is likelier to be understated than overstated, and the open question the two bracketing numbers leave is whether a targeted oral oncolytic rebates anywhere near the company average at all. column11: the programme is finished and failed. KRYSTAL-10 (NCT04793958, 461 patients with KRAS G12C-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer after first-line fluoropyrimidine doublet) missed both its dual primary endpoints, reported at the ESMO Gastrointestinal Cancers Congress 2026: median progression-free survival by blinded independent central review 7.5 months with adagrasib plus cetuximab against 8.1 months with chemotherapy (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.13, p=0.32), and median overall survival 21.6 against 21.7 months (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.03, p=0.09) at a minimum 26.4 months of follow-up. Objective response was higher, 47% against 16%, and did not carry the endpoints. The FDA then withdrew the accelerated approval of adagrasib with cetuximab in previously treated KRAS G12C mCRC, and the current label (DailyMed SPL effective 23 October 2026) no longer carries it
column12: nil, not pending. No pool is seeded for a programme that has already failed. This is also a fact about the base rather than the layer: the 205mm USD revenue anchor was earned partly in an indication the product no longer has
